headline: High-risk pair: broad-egress openagent can leak data and act on unverified outputs from a docs-only data-engineering course artifact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable course repo with no shared channel, so direct injection into B is not documented. Agent B uses runtime-injected MCPs/hooks and parses files like AGENTS.md/README.md, so manual copy-paste or shared-file bridges could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF operator copies A-generated text into B's prompt or workspace files, injection becomes possible.
IF B is configured to ingest shared files from A's repo, attacker-controlled instructions can be parsed.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of repo text into B.
Review copied snippets before pasting into B.
Use read-only mounts for A when B is active.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B has broad egress, browser access, and handles session history, project code, and provider auth prompts. If A's outputs or files are placed into B's context, B can transmit them to third parties by default. The interaction is inferred from B's documented surfaces; A contributes little direct leakage risk.
conditions: IF A outputs are pasted into B's session history or workspace, B may exfiltrate them via external APIs.
IF B is allowed to browse or call APIs on A-derived content, that content can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive A-derived text into B.
Disable B network access for sensitive sessions.
Restrict B API keys to least privilege.
Use a separate workspace for A artifacts.
Clear B session history after handling A content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces documented, while B has subprocesses, browser access, and multiple-instance support with per-installation sessions. There is no documented shared mutable resource between them, so direct write conflict is not evidenced. Uncertainty remains because A's I/O surfaces are empty and could hide unmodeled overlap, so the higher plausible level is not justified.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF B is granted write access to A's repo checkout, subprocess-driven edits may race with manual changes.
mitigations: Keep A read-only.
Do not share a writable workspace.
Run B in a separate installation profile.
Use git branches for any edits.
Lock the directory before B edits files.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a docs-only course repo, so its outputs are likely instructional rather than authoritative facts. B can create messages and task actions, and its tool-use pattern can operationalize content without a built-in verification step. If A-derived text is treated as guidance, B may propagate mistakes into downstream actions; the pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived text as authoritative instructions, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF B sends team messages or creates tasks from unverified A content, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A content.
Mark A content as non-authoritative in prompts.
Add a verification checklist before task creation.
Limit B to drafting, not executing, on A-derived inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repo with no data classes touched, so compliance exposure is minimal. B handles provider auth prompts, installation identifiers, and session history, which can create retention or residency concerns if sensitive content is routed through its APIs. Because A itself is not a regulated-data processor here, only B needs citation; the pairwise compliance risk is limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into B, its external API calls may create residency or retention obligations.
IF provider auth prompts are stored in B session history, local retention policy must cover them.
mitigations: Do not enter regulated data into B.
Review B retention settings.
Separate auth prompts from project work.
Use a local-only profile for sensitive sessions.
